source_text: {ΚΥΡ.} Διὰ νομικῆς οὖν ἄρα λατρείας ἀπρόσιτος ὁ Πατὴρ, μετὰ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ τελείωσιν, προσιτὸς δέ ἐστι διὰ μόνου τοῦ Υἱοῦ. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἔφασκεν, «Οὐδεὶς ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα, εἰ μὴ δι' ἐμοῦ.» Ὅτι δὲ ἄθυτόν τε καὶ ἀτελὲς πᾶν εἴτι μὴ ἐν Χριστῷ, δεκτὸν δὲ καὶ ἱερώτατον τὸ δι' αὐτοῦ τε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ, σαφὲς ἂν γένοιτο καὶ δι' ὧν ὁ νόμος ἐν μὲν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ φησίν· «Οὐχ ἑψήσεις ἄρνα ἐν γάλακτι μητρὸς αὐτοῦ·» ἐν δὲ τῷ Λευιτικῷ· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν λέγων· Μόσχον ἢ πρόβατον ἢ αἶγα ᾧ ἂν τεχθῇ, καὶ ἔσται ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας ὑπὸ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ. Τῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ καὶ ἐπέκεινα, δεχθήσεται εἰς δῶρα κάρπωμα τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ μόσχον καὶ πρόβατον, αὐτὴν καὶ τὸ παιδίον αὐτῆς οὐ σφάξετε ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ.» Ἄρνα μὲν οὖν τὸ ἀρτιγενὲς καὶ ὑπότιτθον ἔτι σφράττειν οὐκ ἐᾷ, δεικνὺς ὅτι, τὸ ἀτελὲς ἔτι καὶ ὡς ἐν συνέσει βραχύ τε καὶ ἀσθενὲς, οὔπω μὲν ἱερόν· ἔτι δὲ ἀπαράδεκτον διὰ τοῦτο Θεῷ. Τοιοῦτοί τινες ἦσαν ἄσοφοί τε καὶ ὀλιγογνώμονες, πρὸς οὓς ὁ θεσπέσιος γράφει Παῦλος· «Καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον, πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκοντος ὑμᾶς τίνα τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος, οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς· τελείων δέ ἐστιν ἡ στερεὰ τροφή.» Οὐκοῦν ἀτελὲς ἔτι, τὸ ἐν γάλακτί τε καὶ ὑπὸ μαστὸν, κατά γε τὸ ἐν συνέσει φημὶ καὶ εὐρωστίᾳ πνευματικῇ· ἴτω δὲ αὖ ἡμῖν ὁ περὶ τῶνδε λόγος, ὡς ἐκ τύπου τῶν ἐν αἰσθήσει καὶ ἐναργῶν πραγμάτων, ἐπὶ τὰ ὑπὲρ αἴσθησίν τε καὶ νοητὰ, πλὴν ὅτι τὰ πάντα γέγονεν ἐν Χριστῷ καὶ ἐν τελειότητι καὶ παραδοχῇ, συνήσεις εὖ μάλα. Τὰ γάρ τοι προσκομιζόμενα ζῶα καὶ ἀνατιθέμενα τῷ Θεῷ, δεῖν μὲν εἶναί φησιν ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας ὑπὸ τὴν μητέρα, τῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ καὶ ἐπέκεινα, δῶρον ἔσεσθαι, καὶ εἰς κάρπωμα τῷ Θεῷ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὐ σφόδρα σαφὴς ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἦ γὰρ οὐχὶ τὴν ὀγδόην τὴν ἀναστάσιμον τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμέραν εἶναι φὴς, καὶ ἀρχὴν ὥσπερ αἰῶνος νέου, παριππεύσαντος τοῦ κατὰ νόμον ὡς ἐν ἡμέραις ἑπτὰ ταῖς πρώταις; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Φημί. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἀνίερόν τε καὶ ἀπροσκόμιστον ἔτι τὸ ὡς ἐν χρόνῳ τῷ κατὰ τὸν νόμον δηλονότι τὸ ἐν λατρείᾳ σαρκικῇ· δῶρον δὲ ἤδη καὶ εὐπρόσδεκτον τῷ Θεῷ πᾶν εἴτι λοιπὸν ἐν Χριστῷ κατὰ τὴν ὀγδόην καὶ ἐπέκεινα. Ἀκατάληκτος γὰρ ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ κλῆσις, ἀρχὴν ἔχουσα τὴν ἀνάστασιν. Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδὼς αὐτὸς ἔφασκεν ὁ Υἱὸς, ὁτὲ μὲν, «Ὅταν ὑψωθῶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς, πάντας ἑλκύσω πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν,» ὁτὲ δὲ, «Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ ὁ κόκκος πεσὼν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἀποθάνῃ, αὐτὸς μόνος μένει· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ, καρπὸν πλείονα φέρει.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. Τὸ δέ γε μὴ συνδιόλλυσθαι
pass_a_gloss: Cyril: Through legal (νομικός) worship (λατρεία) then the Father is unapproachable (ἀπρόσιτος), after the perfecting (τελείωσις) in Christ, but approachable (προσιτός) through the Son alone. Therefore he said: No one comes to the Father except through me. That all that is not in Christ is unsacrificed (ἄθυτος) and imperfect (ἀτελής), but what is through him and in him acceptable (δεκτός) and most holy (ἱερώτατος), would become clear also through what the law says, in Exodus: You shall not boil (ἕψω) a lamb (ἀρήν) in its mother's milk (γάλα); in Leviticus: And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Calf (μόσχος) or sheep or goat, whenever it is born, shall be seven days under its mother; on the eighth day and beyond it will be accepted (δέχομαι) for gifts (δῶρα), a burnt-offering (κάρπωμα) to the Lord; and calf and sheep, it and its young (παιδίον), you shall not slaughter (σφάζω) on one day. The lamb newborn (ἀρτιγενής) and still suckling (ὑπότιτθος) he does not allow to be slaughtered, showing that the still imperfect, and as in understanding (σύνεσις) small and weak, is not yet sacred (ἱερός), still unacceptable (ἀπαράδεκτος) to God for this reason. Such were certain unwise (ἄσοφος) and small-minded (ὀλιγογνώμων) people, to whom the divine (θεσπέσιος) Paul writes: [Hebrews 5:12-14: ought to be teachers by the time, need someone to teach the elements (στοιχεῖα) of the beginning of the oracles (λόγια) of God, become needing milk not solid (στερεός) food; solid food is of the perfect (τέλειοι)]. So imperfect still is what is in milk and under the breast (μαστός), I mean in understanding and spiritual vigor (εὐρωστία πνευματική). Let the account go, as from a type (τύπος) of sensible (ἐν αἰσθήσει) and evident (ἐναργής) things, to things beyond sense and intelligible (νοητά); except that all things have come to be in Christ in perfection (τελειότης) and acceptance (παραδοχή), you will understand well. The animals brought (προσκομίζω) and dedicated (ἀνατίθημι) to God must be seven days under the mother, on the eighth day and beyond be a gift and for burnt-offering to God. Palladius: Not very clear the account. Cyril: Do you not say the eighth (ὀγδόη) is the resurrection-day (ἀναστάσιμος ἡμέρα) of the Savior, and beginning as of a new age (αἰὼν νέος), the [time] according to law, as in seven first days, having ridden past (παριππεύω)? Palladius: I say so. Cyril: Then unholy (ἀνίερος) and not-to-be-offered (ἀπροσκόμιστος) still is what is as in the time according to the law, namely what is in fleshly worship (λατρεία σαρκική); but gift and well-acceptable (εὐπρόσδεκτος) to God already is everything henceforth in Christ according to the eighth and beyond. For unceasing (ἀκατάληκτος) the calling (κλῆσις) in Christ, having resurrection as beginning. Knowing this the Son said, at one time: When I am lifted up (ὑψόω) from the earth I will draw (ἕλκω) all to myself; at another: Amen I say to you, unless the grain (κόκκος) falling into the earth dies, it remains alone; if it dies it bears more (πλείων) fruit. Palladius: You spoke rightly. But that [the mother] must not be destroyed together (συνδιόλλυμαι)... [continues in section 28].
pass_b_english: Cyril: So then, after the perfecting in Christ, the Father cannot be approached through the worship of the law; he can be approached through the Son alone. That is why he said, ‘No one comes to the Father except through me’ (John 14:6). And that everything not in Christ is unfit for sacrifice and imperfect, while what is through him and in him is acceptable and most holy, can also be seen clearly from what the law says. In Exodus it says, ‘You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk’ (Exodus 23:19); and in Leviticus, ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: When a calf or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall be seven days under its mother; but from the eighth day on it shall be accepted as gifts, an offering by fire to the Lord. And a calf or a sheep, the mother and her young, you shall not slaughter on the same day’ (Leviticus 22:26–28). So he does not allow a lamb that is newborn and still at the breast to be slaughtered, showing that what is still immature and, so to speak, small and weak in understanding is not yet holy, and for this reason is still unacceptable to God. Such were certain unwise and small-minded people to whom the inspired Paul writes: ‘For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you again the first principles of the oracles of God; you have come to need milk, not solid food. But solid food belongs to the mature’ (Hebrews 5:12–14). What is still on milk and at the breast is therefore immature, I mean in understanding and in spiritual strength. But let our discussion of these matters now move, as from a type drawn from things that are seen and plain to the senses, to things beyond the senses and grasped by the mind; only, you will understand very well that in Christ all things have come to perfection and acceptance. For the animals that are brought and dedicated to God must, he says, be seven days under their mother, but from the eighth day on they will be a gift, and an offering by fire to God.
Palladius: Your point is not very clear.

Cyril: Do you not say that the eighth day is the day of the Savior’s resurrection, and the beginning, as it were, of a new age, once the time of the law, figured in the first seven days, has passed by?

Cyril: Then whatever belongs, so to speak, to the time of the law, that is, whatever lies in worship according to the flesh, is still unholy and cannot yet be offered; but from now on everything in Christ, on the eighth day and after, is already a gift and well pleasing to God. For the calling in Christ has no end, and its beginning is the resurrection. The Son himself knew this, and so he said at one time, ‘When I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself’ (John 12:32), and at another, ‘Truly I tell you, unless the grain falls into the ground and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears more fruit’ (John 12:24).
Palladius: You have spoken rightly. But the rule that a mother must not be killed…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Exodus 23:19 is cited; the same LXX words recur at Exodus 34:26 (and Deuteronomy 14:21), so the reference could be either Exodus place. Cyril says the law 'does not allow the lamb to be slaughtered', blending the Exodus milk rule with the Leviticus seven-day rule; kept as he wrote it. κάρπωμα rendered 'offering by fire' (LXX term for a burnt portion). Leviticus 22:28 in Cyril's text reads 'calf and sheep, it and its young'; rendered 'calf or sheep, the mother and her young' for sense, since αὐτήν is feminine (the dam). John 12:24: Cyril has πλείονα ('more fruit') where John has πολύν ('much fruit'); followed Cyril. The eighth day as the resurrection day is Cyril's reading, not a Scripture citation; the 'new age' idea carries no citation. The section ends mid-sentence in Palladius' question; it continues in section 28.

changes: ἀτελές rendered 'imperfect'/'immature' to keep the link with Hebrews' 'mature' (τελείων)
'worship of the flesh' -> 'worship according to the flesh' (avoids misreading)
'let our account pass' -> 'let our discussion now move' (pass read as skip)
word order smoothed in 'in Christ all things have come to perfection'
